findings.title: `sq --version` probe breaks the CLI start path under the test stub
findings.description: The new stub `sq` answers *every* command that is not `runs wait` or `run` with the prune path, which requires `SQ_STUB_MODE` in the environment and exits 1 with "stub sq: unexpected arguments" when the mode is absent. `standard_tenants()` calls `capture_sq_version_label()` at start-up (`src/amoeba/process/version_label.py:71`), which runs `sq --version`. Under `cli_environment()` (`tests/cli_harness.py:57`) `SQ_STUB_MODE` is never set, so this call now exits non-zero and the version label becomes `VERSION_UNAVAILABLE` rather than a real label. The label is stored on every review-detection record, so detection rows written under the CLI harness now carry `unavailable` instead of the stub's version. The version label is documented as opaque provenance, so this does not change control flow, but it is a silent degradation introduced by the stub change and is not asserted anywhere. The stub should handle `--version` explicitly (as `tests/detection_e2e_harness.py:102` already does for its own fake `sq`), or `SQ_STUB_MODE` should have a default in `cli_environment()`.

findings.title: Observer state is shared across projects, so one project's entries can be evicted by another's
`_within_grace` raises `ValueError` on a naive `issued_at`, aborting the whole project tick
findings.description:
```python
issued_at = entry.issued_at
if issued_at is None or issued_at.tzinfo is None:
    raise ValueError(f"entry {entry.id} has no timezone-aware issued_at")
```
This raises out of `observe()` into `ProjectTick.run()`, and the Runner tenant's broad catch turns it into an "unexpected fault" escalation for the whole project — the node is not blocked and no run is observed, so every remaining in-flight run for that project is skipped for that tick. The recovery observer handles exactly this case correctly and explicitly, returning `Unknown` with a reason rather than raising (`src/amoeba/process/observers/sq_run_id.py:127-136`). The Runner should treat a naive or missing `issued_at` the same way: an expected fault recorded in `TickFaults` (or a project-scoped escalation), not an exception that aborts the tick.

findings.title: The Runner's process-boundary paths have no load test
findings.description: The Python rules require that code on the simulation, network, concurrency, or environment-layer paths has at least one load test exercising a realistic configuration, and CI must gate load tests for slices touching those paths (`tests/load` is a separate CI step, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`). This slice adds a tenant that launches detached subprocesses, polls them, and reaps children — precisely the concurrency/process-boundary class the rule names. The new `tests/runner/test_crash_recovery.py` covers crash *correctness* but is not a load test: it asserts functional end states, not latency, throughput, or resource bounds, and runs a single node. No file under `tests/load/` references the Runner (`grep` for `runner|Runner|sq run|launch` in `tests/load` returns only unrelated matches), so the Runner's launch/poll/reap cycle is never exercised under repetition. The existing `tests/load/test_crash_loop.py` uses the pre-Runner `JOURNALING_TENANT` stand-in and so does not cover this path.

findings.title: The `sq` outcome exit-code table is duplicated between the store-facing contract and the test stub
findings.description: `tests/sq_stub.py` keeps its own `STUB_EXIT_CODES` mapping and `src/amoeba/process/sq_outcome.py:40` keeps `OUTCOME_EXIT_CODES`. The duplication is deliberate and documented (the stub "is a separate program"), and it is the right call for a test double — but it is a second place where the outcome vocabulary can drift, and the project rule "Never scatter comparison values across code" applies to the production side. Since the stub is a separate program, this is informational only; the production table remains the single source.

findings.title: `PARAM_CHECKOUT` is defined in two modules with the same name
findings.description: `PARAM_CHECKOUT` is defined in `amoeba.store.journal_models` (as `PARAM_CHECKOUT`) and re-exported, while `src/amoeba/runner/launch.py:132` defines its own `PARAM_PIPELINE` and `PARAM_PARAMS` constants for the sibling journal keys that *are* exported by the store (`PARAM_RUN_ID` is). The three keys describe one journal-parameter vocabulary split across two owners. `PARAM_PIPELINE`/`PARAM_PARAMS` are already duplicated by `src/amoeba/process/observers/sq_runs.py:42-43`, so this is a pre-existing pattern rather than a new inconsistency — but the store already owns `PARAM_RUN_ID` and `PARAM_CHECKOUT`, and adding the remaining two there would give the Runner one import rather than three.

findings.title: The Runner's subprocess calls are all budget-guarded, and the guard is mechanically tested
findings.description: I verified each call site against `TickBudget.allows_call()`: the poll (`src/amoeba/runner/observe.py:160`), the `cf` probe (`src/amoeba/runner/probes.py:139`), and the `Popen` (`src/amoeba/runner/tick.py:176`). `tests/runner/test_budget_coverage.py` wraps all three with a guard that fails the test if a call begins after the deadline, which is the mechanical enforcement the D10 claim requires.

findings.title: The broad exception handler is confined, documented, and re-raises store failures
findings.description: The single `except Exception` in the package is at the documented process boundary, carries an inline justification for the `BLE001` suppression, logs via `logger.exception`, and re-raises `STORE_FAILURES` and `UpstreamShapeError` so the process exits rather than running blind. `tests/runner/test_tenant.py:190` asserts the package contains exactly one such handler, and `src/amoeba/store/models.py:162-198` confirms `StoreBusyError`, `StoreCorruptError`, `StorePermissionError` and `StoreSchemaError` are distinct exception types covered by that tuple.

findings.title: Journal-before-side-effect ordering holds on the launch path
findings.description: `_launch()` calls `build_argv()` for validation *before* `journal_issue()`, then journals, then launches — and `finish.record()` resolves the entry when the launch fails, so a failed launch does not leave a dangling entry. `tests/runner/test_tick.py:43` asserts the entry is committed before the `Popen` call by counting unresolved entries at call time, and `tests/runner/test_crash_recovery.py:47` proves the "killed before launch" case resolves as `NOT_APPLIED` by recovery without any relaunch.
